source.title: Branch-specific dendritic Ca(2+) spikes cause persistent synaptic plasticity

confidence_rationale: Nature-tier in vivo two-photon imaging with a CAUSAL manipulation that removes the bounding mechanism and produces exactly the failure MECH-471 predicts: prior motor competence is disrupted by learning a second task. Discounted for mapping -- the two tasks are both forelimb motor tasks in the same cortical region, so 'unrelated' here is weaker than MECH-471's 'unrelated previously-acquired competences', and the bounding is biophysical (dendritic compartmentalisation) with no direct REE analogue.
failure_signatures: When somatostatin-expressing interneurons are inactivated, different motor tasks stop being routed to different apical tuft branches and instead frequently induce Ca2+ spikes on the SAME branches -- i.e. the scope bound on the competence update is removed.

On those shared branches, spines potentiated during one task are DEPOTENTIATED when active seconds before Ca2+ spikes induced by another task: a later update silently overwrites the substrate of an earlier competence.
The overwrite is behaviourally consequential, not merely synaptic -- increased neuronal activity and the performance improvement after learning one task are disrupted when another task is learned.
The protective mechanism is inhibitory and therefore FAILABLE: competence isolation is not a static property of the substrate but an actively maintained gate that can be switched off.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Different motor learning tasks induce dendritic Ca2+ spikes on different apical tuft branches of individual layer V motor cortex pyramidal neurons; this branch-specific segregation causes long-lasting potentiation of co-active spines, and when the segregation is abolished by inactivating SST interneurons, learning a second task depotentiates the first task's spines and disrupts the first task's learned performance gain.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the biological instantiation of MECH-471's core assertion. The brain does NOT permit a behavioural-competence update to write wherever gradient pressure points; it enforces a scope bound (which dendritic branch may be written) as a precondition for storing a new competence without destroying an existing one. The SST-inactivation condition is a live, causal instance of MECH-471's proposed LOCAL-UPDATE INTERFERENCE TEST run in reverse -- remove the bound, and previously acquired competence degrades measurably. In MECH-471's polarity that is a FAIL, i.e. the outcome that MOTIVATES building the discipline. It also satisfies the claim's own NON-DEGENERACY GUARD: the interfered-with competence was demonstrably acquired (a measured performance improvement existed before the second task was learned), so this is not interference measured against a competence the animal never had.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Three boundaries. (1) The two tasks are both forelimb motor tasks encoded in the same cortical region -- adjacent, not 'unrelated' in MECH-471's sense; the paper therefore evidences interference at CLOSER competence distance than the claim's falsifier specifies, which if anything makes it a weaker test of the general case. (2) The bounding mechanism is biophysical compartmentalisation of a dendritic tree, which has no structural counterpart in REE's competence substrate (action objects, learned affordances, goal-conditioned policies); the transfer is at the level of DESIGN PRINCIPLE -- update scope must be bounded -- not implementation. (3) The paper speaks only to BOUNDING. It says nothing about provenance records or rollback, the other two properties MECH-471 registers, so it cannot be read as support for the claim's full triple.
mapping.source_context: Mouse (male and female) motor cortex, layer V pyramidal neurons; in vivo two-photon Ca2+ imaging of apical tuft dendrites and spines during two distinct forelimb motor learning tasks; causal test via inactivation of somatostatin-expressing interneurons.

confidence_components.notes: Weighted toward mapping_fidelity because MECH-471 is an architectural/discipline claim rather than an empirical one about mice. Source quality is high (Nature, causal manipulation, in vivo) but this is single-lab work and the behavioural disruption is the least-replicated part of the result.
